w: Five Archbishops of Canterbury are buried in this Addington churchyard, a legacy of the 19th century when the archbishops lived next door at Addington Palace. The parish church became, for decades, the private chapel of the Church of England's most senior office.
s: Churchyard resting place of five archbishops
_facts: Five Archbishops of Canterbury are buried here
Addington Palace next door was the archbishops' 19th-century residence

w: King George V ceremonially opened one of the first houses on this 522-acre LCC cottage estate in 1927, designed by architect George Topham Forrest to rehouse Londoners from slum conditions after the First World War. Most of its acreage lies in Lewisham, with a slice in the old Municipal Borough of Bromley.
s: Interwar cottage estate opened by George V
_facts: Built 1924-1930 to plans by George Topham Forrest
One of its first houses opened by King George V in 1927
Covered 522 acres, mostly in Lewisham with a share in Bromley

w: Bromley Town Hall has stood on Tweedy Road since 1906, a municipal building serving as the seat of local government for the London Borough of Bromley. Grade II listed, it remains a solid example of early twentieth-century civic architecture in the heart of the town.
